newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa enjoyed an export bonanza in October, with the weak rand and a surge in diamond sales pushing the trade surplus to a record 3.9 billion rand.

- The Wheat Board secured an urgent interdict against agricultural marketing company Propermark in the Bloemfontein Supreme Court on Monday, effectively barring it from buying or selling wheat or any other commodity linked to the single-channel winter grain scheme.

- Diversified industrial holding group Rembrandt Group Ltd reported a 50 percent surge in attributable income to one billion rand in the six months to September, benefitting from good profit from its tobacco business and an exceptional capital surplus on the sale of its hardware timber interests and other investments and assets.
- Eastern Cape premier Ray Mhlaba is expected to announce his resignation on Thursday.
- The leader of the African National Congress' Free State task team, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni, announced a timetable for the election of a cabinet and party leader for the province.

- A sparkling performance by South Africa's exporters pushed the October trade account to a record monthly surplus of 3.9 billion rand, radically changing the outlook for the current account and interest rates next year.

- The Rembrandt Group Ltd, the tobbaco and industrial conglomerate, reported a better-than-expected 36.5 percent increase in net income before exceptional items to 950 million rand in the six months to September 30.
- National Chick Ltd, the day old broiler-chick producer, bucked the negative trend in the industry by posting a 45 percent rise in attributable profit to 10.6 million for the year to September 30.

- Cyril Ramaphosa, Johnnies Industrial Corporation Ltd's (Johnnic) newly appointed chairman, said he looked forward to discussions with Caxton Ltd on his return from Australia about threatened action by Caxton against Omni Media Corporation Ltd, which he recently took over through the acquisition of Johnnic.
- Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd, which secured a controlling stake in JCI Ltd last week, is set to acquire Seeff Holdings Ltd, the listed property and financial services group.
- Gauteng education department authorities are closing in on matric exam cheats, and scores of matriculants from up to 22 schools are likely to be called to explain themselves.

- A 26-year-old Mbazwana man on Monday told a court in Ubombo, KwaZulu-Natal, how he had hacked and stabbed two women to death in 1992 on a remote beach in Sodwana on the Maputaland coast before dumping their bodies in the sea.
